title: Preparatory acts: sense of sin, fear, faith, hope
source_text: XVII. Tales actus ad veram justitiam & sanctitatem dispositorii seu praeparatorii sunt peccati sensus atque agnitio, timor judicii divini, propositum vitae melioris, & anteactae vitae odium & detestatio; tum veniae spes quaedam & misericordiae divinae fiducia, aliqua etiam Dei dilectio, in primis vero fides efficax atque actuosa, ex qua spes, dilectio, & fiducia illa oriuntur. Nam priusquam homo accipiat Spiritum sancti-ficationis, & internam illam gratiam per quam anima renovatur, & Christianis virtuti-bus ornatur, secundum ordinem a Deo constitutum, & legem ab eo positam, necesse est illum verbo Dei credere, & timore perculsum, deque peccatis attritum & dolentem, ad misericordiam divinam confugere cum proposito vitae emendandae, & a peccatis in posterum abstinendi.
pass_a_gloss: Such acts disposing or preparatory to true righteousness and holiness are the sense and acknowledgment of sin, fear of divine judgment, purpose of a better life, and hatred and detestation of the life previously led; then a certain hope of pardon and trust in divine mercy, some love of God also, and above all efficacious and active faith, from which that hope, love, and trust arise. For before a man receives the Spirit of sanctification and that internal grace by which the soul is renewed and adorned with Christian virtues, according to the order constituted by God and the law he has set, it is necessary that he believe the Word of God and, struck with fear and contrite and grieving for sins, flee to divine mercy with purpose of amending his life and thereafter abstaining from sins.
pass_b_english: Preparatory acts: sense and acknowledgment of sin, fear of judgment, purpose of better life, hatred of past sin, some hope and trust, love, above all efficacious faith.
Before sanctifying Spirit and habitual grace, one must believe, be stricken, and flee to mercy intending amendment.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1051.
